fills.researcher_notes: Same company-level Operator question as P0271 and P3669 -- resolved once for the whole Transco brief per gotcha 4, see full reasoning on P0271. Doubly relevant here: the FERC certificate order CP16-494 that is the second independent source IS the order that approved THIS project (Gulf Connector Expansion), naming Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC (Transco) as the applicant/certificate holder throughout.

validity.recommendation: Leave Diameter blank as recorded -- Gulf Connector is a compressor-station and interconnect expansion with no new mainline pipe diameter to record; LengthKnownKm=0 is already correct. No action needed.
validity.researcher_notes: FERC's certificate order (Docket CP16-494, issued Nov 21, 2017, https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-08/CP16-494.pdf, downloaded and read with pdftotext -layout -- the word 'diameter' does not appear anywhere in the 20-page order) authorizes 'the construction and operation of three new compressor stations, a new pipeline interconnect, and modifications to two existing compressor stations' -- three compressor stations (CS17 San Patricio Co, CS23 Victoria Co, CS32 Wharton Co, TX, 30,650 hp total), a new interconnect with Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline, and in-station 'piping and valve modifications' at two existing compressor stations to enable bi-directional flow. No new mainline pipe segment is authorized anywhere in the order. Second, independent source: Natural Gas Intelligence's contemporaneous coverage confirms the same compressor/interconnect-only scope (https://www.naturalgasintel.com/transcos-lng-focused-gulf-connector-gets-favorable-ea/). Per the standing compression-only rule, the sheet's blank Diameter is the correct, confirmed value; the wiki's combined diameter list (20/30/36/42 in) belongs to other Transco projects in the same infobox, not to Gulf Connector.
